text:
alex: ran a quick nsys capture on the new batching rollout, attaching the trace: https://internal.nsys/1789001234
jess: thanks — any specific workload? small-chat baseline or long-context? :eyes:
mohit: small-chat baseline with kv-prefetch enabled (batch size 4, seq len 1024). seeing weird idle gaps on CPU side during prefetch.
alex: exact command i used:
```
nsys profile --output trace_1789001234 --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi python -m server.batcher --cfg smallchat
```
lia: skimmed the waterfall — big host->device memcpy spikes right before `attention_kv_cache_prefetch_kernel` starts. memcpys occupy copy engine and seem to serialize kernels on default streams.
perf-bot: analysis suggestion: check pinned vs pageable host allocation, and whether we’re using `cuMemcpyAsync` on non-overlapped streams.
alex: good point. our prefetch uses `memcpy` wrapper that may fall back to synchronous `cudaMemcpy` on some code paths.
mohit: confirmed: trace shows `cuMemcpy` events on stream 0 and kernels on stream 1 waiting ~1.8ms frequently. CPU shows scheduling gaps ~2-10ms correlating with memcpy bursts.
jess: do we pin memory before prefetch? that's usually the common root cause for host stall.
alex: older batcher path uses `new/alloc` without cudaHostAlloc. new path uses pinned, but not in the rollout path — i missed that flag.
lia: that explains the serialization. Also see many tiny memcpys (128KB-ish) instead of aggregating into larger buffered copy.
mohit: tiny copies + pageable mem => CPU pinned for copy glue -> cpu preemption visible in nsight timeline.
sam: short suggestion: 1) switch prefetch alloc to cudaHostAlloc/pinned, 2) aggregate per-request small copies into single batched memcpy per GPU, 3) use explicit streams with higher priority for kernels vs copy engine separation.
alex: do we have a quick patch to test pinned alloc? I can throw a feature flag and run another capture.
jess: also consider using `cudaMemcpyAsync` onto non-blocking streams and make sure stream priorities separate compute vs copy if multi-engine available.
mohit: one more nuance: on T4-like hosts copy engine may still block compute if memcopy is on default stream and not peer-aware. need to ensure `cudaMemcpyAsync` + `cudaHostAlloc` + `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` pattern.
lia: for diagnostic, run `nsys stats --report=timeline,driver,syscalls trace_1789001234.qdrep` and grep for "cuMemcpy" peaks; also enable NVTX ranges around prefetch to see batching alignment.
alex: running a second capture now with pinned=True and batching combined. command updated to:
```
PYTHONFLAGS=... nsys profile --output trace_1789001234_pinned --sample=none python -m server.batcher --cfg smallchat --prefetch pinned --prefetch-batch 8
```
perf-bot: quick metric note: pinned path reduced host CPU time by ~60% in a local run, per micro-benchmarks.
sam: if pinned solves it we should also add a heuristic: if avg prefetch memcpy < 512KB, batch N requests until buffer >= 512KB or timeout 2ms.
jess: agreed. also capture another trace with `--trace-processes` to confirm stream ownership across threads.
mohit: one oddity left: even with pinned copies there's still occasional 200-300us kernel stalls where kernel waits for copy engine — possibly due to GPU compute vs copy engine contention. could be kernel scheduling or kernel launching on low-priority stream.
lia: try increasing compute stream priority via `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority` and keep copy engine on default stream. that'll bias scheduling.
alex: i pushed a quick branch `prefetch/pinned-batched` with the alloc flag and batching heuristic, running in QA now.
jess: will review the trace when it's done. if this fixes regression we should roll to canary with perf regression guard.
alex: thanks all — i'll post new nsys link when available.
sam: nice triage. follow-ups: alex (run canary trace + attach nvtx), jess (add heuristic PR), mohit (write perf microbench), lia (run priority experiment on staging GPU). :thumbsup:
alex: acked. back in a bit with results.
